desc:
The string expr is an expression without spaces made of non-negative integer literals, the binary operators +, -, * and round brackets. There are no unary operators.

This calculator does not use the usual priorities. The array prio has three values: prio[0] is the priority of +, prio[1] of - and prio[2] of *. An operator with a higher priority number is applied before one with a lower number; operators with equal priority are applied from left to right. Brackets always override priorities.

Return the value of the expression modulo 1,000,000,007, as a number from 0 to 1,000,000,006 (also when the true value is negative).

Examples: for 2+3*4 with prio = [1, 1, 2] (the usual rules) the answer is 14; with prio = [2, 2, 1] it is (2+3)*4 = 20. For 10-3+2 with prio = [2, 1, 3] the + goes first: 10-(3+2) = 5.
constraints: expr is a valid expression with literals in [0, 10<sup>9</sup>] without leading zeros (except "0") and balanced brackets
hints: With the normal rules you would use two stacks (numbers and operators). The only thing that changes here is how two operators are compared.
Keep a stack of values and a stack of pending operators. Before pushing a new operator, apply the pending operators on top that must be evaluated first.

Apply the top operator while it is not a ( and its priority is greater than or equal to the new one (equal means left to right). A ) applies everything down to its (. Do all arithmetic modulo 109+7: the operations +, -, * stay correct under a modulus.
editorial: This is the shunting-yard evaluation with priorities taken from a table instead of being hard-coded. Scan the string: a number is pushed on the value stack; ( is pushed on the operator stack; for ) apply operators until the matching ( and drop it.

For an operator c: while the operator stack is not empty, its top is not ( and pr[top] >= pr[c], apply the top (pop two values a, b, push a top b). Using >= makes equal priorities left-associative. Then push c. After the scan apply everything that is left; the single remaining value is the answer.

Addition, subtraction and multiplication are ring operations, so every intermediate result can be reduced modulo 109+7 without changing the final remainder. In Python % already returns a non-negative number. Time O(n), space O(n).
